Answer: C
Reason: The yellow arrow points to a prominent left superior mediastinal contour, which is the classic radiographic sign of a persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC). When a PLSVC drains directly into the left atrium (unroofed coronary sinus), it causes a right-to-left shunt leading to hypoxaemia without pulmonary congestion, matching the clinical picture and clear lung fields.
